approval_source.question_set: Hetzner will not raise the account limits; run R03 and T05 with the capacity the account has (user: 'proceed as outlined', then 'fill out with your recommendations', 13 November 2026)

reason: Hetzner refused to raise the account limits. The project has 8 cores, 7 of them in use (the website cpx21, 3; the staging sentry and validator cx23, 2 each), and 2 of its 5 primary IPv4 addresses free. That leaves room for one 1-core load machine. The 7-machine plan in P01_T06_STAGING_3_T9_AND_FLOODS_2026-11-11 created no machines on 11 November (run 20261111155419). While rescoping this, the adapter's per-address connection bound turned out to key on the exact IP, so one IPv6 /64 could fill every slot; fixed in PR #146 (CI only).

decisions.question: Load sources for R03 and T05
decisions.selected: One Hetzner load machine (1 core) for the floods and load; the founder's Mac for the drive and the honest client
decisions.rule: At most 1 load machine per window, made by load_machines.py up --count 1, the cheapest x86 type outside hel1, deleted by the watchdog at its deadline. The founder's Mac runs the drive and the honest client in the r03-drive container, as on 11 November. Both sources use IPv4 only.

decisions.question: R03 transaction floods
decisions.selected: Run as approved in P01_T04_FLOODS_2026-11-09 from the two sources
decisions.rule: Transaction volume depends on the wallet fleet, not the number of source addresses; the flood rules and pass criteria are unchanged.

decisions.question: R03 request floods
decisions.selected: Measure what two IPv4 sources can do; slot exhaustion stays proven in CI
decisions.rule: On the real hosts the run reports sentry latency, throughput and whether the honest client is served while two sources hold their per-address connections. That 14 flooding connections from 7 addresses leave the honest client served is proven by the CI network job (30 of 30 attempts clean on 10 November) and is not claimed from this run.

decisions.question: T05 capacity
decisions.selected: Step the rate from the same sources until the sentry or the load source saturates
decisions.rule: The pass rule of P01_T06_T05_CAPACITY_RUN_2026-11-10 (at least 180 basic Sends a block for 30 minutes, nothing lost) is unchanged. If the load source saturates first, the result is recorded as a lower bound, not a pass, and goes back for a decision.

decisions.question: When R03 runs
decisions.rule: One window for both flood types: with one load machine there is no reason to split them. load_machines.py up --count 1 --hours 4 at 15:00 UTC; 10 transaction floods, then 10 request floods (flood_workers.py drive --workers 1); down at the end, and load_machines.py check must show nothing left. The no-cost preparation (funding preflight, priming) runs before 15:00 with no machine up.

decisions.question: How long the load machine may run
decisions.selected: 4 hours per window, deleted by the watchdog at its deadline
decisions.rule: Each window makes its own machine; none outlives its window.

decisions.question: When the T5 host loss on the real staging sentry runs
decisions.rule: Once, under P01_T05 real-host decisions of 10 November (existing hcloud token, staging sentry only, 600 s target). After R03 so the floods are not measured on a host just power-cycled; before T05. After the boot, timedatectl timesync-status is recorded.

decisions.question: When T05 runs
decisions.rule: One load machine for 4 hours, as for R03.

decisions.question: T05 rate steps
decisions.selected: 60, 120, 180 basic Sends a block for 10 minutes each, then 180 held for 30 minutes, then 240 for 10 minutes
decisions.rule: At the 5 s block target: 12, 24, 36, then 36 held, then 48 transactions a second (load.py --rate). 70 minutes of load inside the window. The 30-minute hold at 180 is the pass rule's measurement; the 240 step reads headroom only and does not change the pass rule. If the load source cannot reach a step, the run stops stepping and records the highest rate reached as a lower bound.

decisions.question: T05 memory and CPU reading
decisions.rule: No resource reading exists in the tools yet and building one would delay the run. The run reports rate, inclusion and losses; the 4 GB server and 3 GiB node-limit check of P01_E05_TWO_SEATS stays open, to be measured in a later T05 run once a reading is built.

accepted_risks: The real-host request flood cannot fill the sentry's connection slots from enough addresses; that property rests on CI.

The staging hosts run bundles built before PR #146, so their per-address bound still keys on the exact IP. Using IPv4-only sources keeps the run unaffected; the fix reaches the hosts with the next sealed bundle.
The founder's Mac is a home connection: its uplink and NAT may cap the rate before the sentry does.
T05 does not yet show the node within its 3 GiB memory limit under load; that check stays open.
The drive and the honest client run in the linux container on the founder's Mac under amd64 emulation; the 120-block transaction expiry and 3 retries (PR #133) cover its slow signing.
supersedes: the 7-machine count and window in P01_T06_STAGING_3_T9_AND_FLOODS_2026-11-11 (the flood rules there still apply)
the machine count (1 to 8) and the 'once the Hetzner IPv4 limit increase is granted' timing in P01_T06_T05_CAPACITY_RUN_2026-11-10
does_not_authorize: more than 1 load machine per window, or any run outside its window
stopping, resizing or deleting the website server or either staging host
load machines at any other provider
rebuilding either host or lifting a host's delete protection
any change to the approved capacity, queue or connection values
